note: Batch g8 (2026-10-14). Groupings and directions by an agent from the claims' titles and evidence entries. The outcomes differ by hub (attitudes towards a group; social-cognitive task scores; social-emotional skill composites; teacher discipline and suspensions) and must not be read as one 'empathy' outcome. Review before applying. reading-literary-fiction-improves-theory-of-mind is left out: it is itself a general claim with three studies and no narrower member in the wiki, and its outcome (social-cognitive task scores) is not the attitude outcome of the first hub.

findings.question: Does structured perspective-taking or contact improve learners' attitudes towards another person or group, and does it reach behaviour?
Do sustained, structured programmes produce social-emotional gains, and do they last?
When the learners are adults who act on others (teachers), does an empathy exercise change their conduct?
